1: import type { GlossaryTerm } from './types.js';
2: 
3: export interface GlossaryMatcher {
4:   /** null when the glossary is empty, or auto-linking is off (`GameSettings.GlossaryAutoLink`)
5:    *  — callers should skip regex matching entirely in that case. Explicit `[Term]` tags (see
6:    *  below) resolve independently of this and keep working either way. */
7:   regex: RegExp | null;
8:   /** Lowercased Name/Alias -> the term it resolves to. */
9:   termByKey: Map<string, GlossaryTerm>;
10:   /** Term `Id` -> the term itself, so an explicit tag's second bracket
11:    *  (`[shaken][g-status]`) can resolve by Id as well as by Name/Alias. */
12:   termById: Map<string, GlossaryTerm>;
13: }
14: 
15: export interface GlossarySegment {
16:   text: string;
17:   /** Set only on segments that matched a term. */
18:   term?: GlossaryTerm;
19: }
20: 
21: /** How many bubble-opens deep a piece of text is being linkified at. 0 is the original
22:  *  sheet text; a term's Definition, shown inside the bubble opened from a depth-0 match, is
23:  *  linkified at depth 1 so a definition that itself uses jargon still helps. Depth 2 is refused
24:  *  so a chain of definitions can't open bubble after bubble. */
25: const MAX_DEPTH = 1;
26: 
27: function escapeRegExp(s: string): string {
28:   return s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
29: }
30: 
31: /** Compiles every Name/Alias across `terms` into one alternation regex, longest phrase first so
32:  *  a multi-word alias ("Mark Kin") wins over a shorter one ("Kin") that's also a substring of it.
33:  *  Matching is case-sensitive and word-bounded on purpose: this game's rules text always
34:  *  capitalizes its proper nouns ("mark a Condition", not "mark a condition"), so requiring the
35:  *  authored casing is what keeps this from linking ordinary English words that happen to share a
36:  *  term's spelling.
37:  *
38:  *  `options.autoLink: false` (from `GameSettings.GlossaryAutoLink`, 0.24.0) retires this regex
39:  *  entirely — `regex` comes back null, same as an empty glossary — while `termByKey`/`termById`
40:  *  stay populated so explicit `[Term]` tags (see `linkifyText`) keep resolving regardless. */
41: export function buildGlossaryMatcher(terms: GlossaryTerm[], options?: { autoLink?: boolean }): GlossaryMatcher {
42:   const termByKey = new Map<string, GlossaryTerm>();
43:   const termById = new Map<string, GlossaryTerm>();
44:   const phrases: string[] = [];
45:   for (const term of terms) {
46:     termById.set(term.Id, term);
47:     for (const raw of [term.Name, ...term.Aliases]) {
48:       const phrase = raw.trim();
49:       if (!phrase) continue;
50:       const key = phrase.toLowerCase();
51:       if (!termByKey.has(key)) termByKey.set(key, term);
52:       phrases.push(phrase);
53:     }
54:   }
55:   const autoLink = options?.autoLink ?? true;
56:   if (phrases.length === 0 || !autoLink) return { regex: null, termByKey, termById };
57: 
58:   const sorted = [...phrases].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length);
59:   const alternation = sorted.map(escapeRegExp).join('|');
60:   return { regex: new RegExp(`\\b(?:${alternation})\\b`, 'g'), termByKey, termById };
61: }
62: 
63: /** Resolves an explicit tag's target string against a matcher: term `Id` first (exact, since
64:  *  Ids are authored lowercase slugs), then Name/Alias (case-insensitive, unlike the regex
65:  *  auto-linker — an author typing an explicit tag shouldn't also have to match authored casing). */
66: function resolveExplicitTag(key: string, matcher: GlossaryMatcher): GlossaryTerm | undefined {
67:   return matcher.termById.get(key) ?? matcher.termByKey.get(key.toLowerCase());
68: }
69: 
70: type TagToken = { kind: 'text'; value: string } | { kind: 'tag'; display: string; resolveKey: string };
71: 
72: /**
73:  * Low-level tokenizer for CommonMark reference-link-style explicit glossary tags, shared by
74:  * `scanExplicitTags` (rendering) and `findUnresolvedGlossaryTags` (Content Admin validation) —
75:  * doesn't know about a glossary at all, just the bracket grammar:
76:  *
77:  *   - `[Kin]`            — a tag; display and resolve-key are both "Kin".
78:  *   - `[shaken][g-kin]`  — display "shaken", resolve-key "g-kin" (a term Id or Name/Alias).
79:  *   - `\[`, `\]`         — a literal bracket, no tag (standard CommonMark escaping).
80:  *
81:  * An unmatched `[` with no closing `]` is left as a literal character rather than treated as a
82:  * malformed tag — authored content must not be able to break a render. `hadBrackets` is true the
83:  * moment any bracket construct is found (a tag or an escape), regardless of whether the tag goes
84:  * on to resolve against a glossary.
85:  */
86: function tokenizeTags(text: string): { tokens: TagToken[]; hadBrackets: boolean } {
87:   const tokens: TagToken[] = [];
88:   let hadBrackets = false;
89:   let plain = '';
90:   let i = 0;
91: 
92:   const flushPlain = () => {
93:     if (plain) tokens.push({ kind: 'text', value: plain });
94:     plain = '';
95:   };
96: 
97:   while (i < text.length) {
98:     const ch = text[i];
99:     if (ch === '\\' && (text[i + 1] === '[' || text[i + 1] === ']')) {
100:       plain += text[i + 1];
101:       hadBrackets = true;
102:       i += 2;
103:       continue;
104:     }
105:     if (ch === '[') {
106:       const close = text.indexOf(']', i + 1);
107:       if (close === -1) {
108:         plain += ch;
109:         i += 1;
110:         continue;
111:       }
112:       const display = text.slice(i + 1, close);
113:       let resolveKey = display;
114:       let end = close + 1;
115:       if (text[end] === '[') {
116:         const close2 = text.indexOf(']', end + 1);
117:         if (close2 !== -1) {
118:           resolveKey = text.slice(end + 1, close2);
119:           end = close2 + 1;
120:         }
121:       }
122:       hadBrackets = true;
123:       flushPlain();
124:       tokens.push({ kind: 'tag', display, resolveKey });
125:       i = end;
126:       continue;
127:     }
128:     plain += ch;
129:     i += 1;
130:   }
131:   flushPlain();
132:   return { tokens, hadBrackets };
133: }
134: 
135: /**
136:  * Scans `text` for explicit glossary tags and resolves each one against `matcher` (see
137:  * `tokenizeTags` for the bracket grammar). Returns `hadExplicit: true` the moment any bracket
138:  * construct is found — see `linkifyText` for why that's the signal that turns off the regex
139:  * auto-linker for the rest of this field, not just the tagged occurrence.
140:  */
141: function scanExplicitTags(
142:   text: string,
143:   matcher: GlossaryMatcher,
144:   excludeTermId?: string,
145: ): { segments: GlossarySegment[]; hadExplicit: boolean } {
146:   const { tokens, hadBrackets } = tokenizeTags(text);
147:   const segments: GlossarySegment[] = tokens.map((t) => {
148:     if (t.kind === 'text') return { text: t.value };
149:     const term = resolveExplicitTag(t.resolveKey, matcher);
150:     return term && term.Id !== excludeTermId ? { text: t.display, term } : { text: t.display };
151:   });
152:   return { segments, hadExplicit: hadBrackets };
153: }
154: 
155: /** Every explicit tag's resolve-key that failed to resolve against `matcher` — used by Content
156:  *  Admin's Validation panel (`validateLibrary`, `apps/server/src/adminLogic.ts`) to surface a
157:  *  typo'd or dangling `[Tag]` at authoring time, per the plan's "an author finds out at authoring
158:  *  time" requirement, rather than it silently rendering as plain text forever. */
159: export function findUnresolvedGlossaryTags(text: string, matcher: GlossaryMatcher): string[] {
160:   const { tokens } = tokenizeTags(text);
161:   const unresolved: string[] = [];
162:   for (const t of tokens) {
163:     if (t.kind === 'tag' && !resolveExplicitTag(t.resolveKey, matcher)) unresolved.push(t.resolveKey);
164:   }
165:   return unresolved;
166: }
167: 
168: /**
169:  * Splits `text` into plain and glossary-matched segments.
170:  *
171:  * `depth` tracks recursion into a term's own Definition (see MAX_DEPTH above) — callers
172:  * rendering top-level sheet text should leave it at the default 0.
173:  *
174:  * `excludeTermId` skips a term when linkifying its own Definition, so a term's bubble never
175:  * contains a tap-target that reopens itself.
176:  *
177:  * Explicit `[Term]`/`[display][id-or-name]` tags (see `scanExplicitTags`, 0.24.0) are checked
178:  * first. **A field containing at least one explicit tag is treated as fully explicit** — the
179:  * regex auto-linker below is skipped for the rest of that field, not just the tagged occurrence.
180:  * That's what makes migrating a field to explicit tags free: no flag, no backfill, a field with
181:  * no brackets behaves exactly as it always has.
182:  */
183: export function linkifyText(
184:   text: string,
185:   matcher: GlossaryMatcher,
186:   depth = 0,
187:   excludeTermId?: string,
188: ): GlossarySegment[] {
189:   if (!text || depth > MAX_DEPTH) return [{ text }];
190: 
191:   const explicit = scanExplicitTags(text, matcher, excludeTermId);
192:   if (explicit.hadExplicit) return explicit.segments.length ? explicit.segments : [{ text: '' }];
193: 
194:   if (!matcher.regex) return [{ text }];
195: 
196:   const segments: GlossarySegment[] = [];
197:   let lastIndex = 0;
198:   matcher.regex.lastIndex = 0;
199:   let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
200:   while ((match = matcher.regex.exec(text))) {
201:     if (match.index > lastIndex) segments.push({ text: text.slice(lastIndex, match.index) });
202:     const term = matcher.termByKey.get(match[0].toLowerCase());
203:     // Excluded (a term's own name inside its own Definition) still renders as plain text —
204:     // only the tap-link is suppressed, the word itself must not disappear from the sentence.
205:     segments.push(term && term.Id !== excludeTermId ? { text: match[0], term } : { text: match[0] });
206:     lastIndex = match.index + match[0].length;
207:   }
208:   if (lastIndex < text.length) segments.push({ text: text.slice(lastIndex) });
209:   return segments.length ? segments : [{ text }];
210: }
